structured_output.summary: Chunk "qualification-and-package" for phase 20 (G25 0.2.2) is delivered and mechanically substantiated at the reviewed source 519219d6. I independently enumerated the full phase-20 gate from tools/check_phase.py:70-87 (commands_for(17)+commands_for(19), deduplicated, plus generate_models --verify-fixtures and both native-export probes) and it is exactly 59 commands; the recorded snapshot docs/reviews/phase-20-chunk-qualification-and-package-attempt-03.checks.json contains those same 59 invocations in order, all exit_code 0, with source_sha256 = 519219d6 and source_unchanged true. No command in the snapshot is unexecuted or timed out. Version is bumped (crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml:3 = 0.2.2). Both clean archive proofs (docs/checks/phase-20-release-package-1.89.0.json / -1.99.0.json) are real executions at releaseCommit 0716cfd with requireClean true, effectiveDirty false, four packaged examples (including the new response_compatibility) and three external-consumer `cargo run --locked` executions each at exit 0; scripts/check-access-release.py then rebinds both proofs to HEAD, re-reads the retained archives, recomputes the file inventory and VCS, and compares every packaged src/examples/legal/manifest byte against both the filesystem and the release commit, so the candidate receipt is not a self-assertion. Contract documentation is complete and generated: docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md is produced by tools/g25_report.py (gate-checked for staleness, corpus digest-bound) and links each of the 47 operations to its actual frozen response expression, the 76 retained caller UUID checks, the rejected query options, the retained numeric/array domains and the time_order refinement; CHANGELOG.md:11-68 states the loosened and retained rules, the --offset/--search usage-error requirement, and explicitly declines consumer-adoption and live-acceptance claims. Regressions are wired into the 49-job matrix and enforced (tools/test_ci.py:111,113-127,461-484), historical gate lists are pinned (tools/test_review_phase.py:20-44), and the phase-19 deferred items are now present: strict starting-witness assertions (crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:92-102), regex metadata validated before response relaxation (crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:1209-1229), the fifth-attempt >40 floor made explicit with category and deficiency conditions (tools/review_phase.py:68-83), and chunk scope/prompt binding (tools/review_phase.py:239-251). The live re-run is genuine and honest: docs/checks/phase-08-live-attempt-14.json records crateVersion 0.2.2, 24 requests, three 403s and two 400s, cleanupState not_needed, sanitized external-registration placeholders, and tools/live_evidence.py --check (executed, exit 0) binds its runtimeInputsSha256 to the current runtime fingerprint, so the live claim cannot drift from the shipped source. Remaining gaps are low-severity bookkeeping: an undisclosed dangling readiness attempt 03, current-release receipt links that cannot yet resolve while the publication document guard is dormant, and operator-run package proofs plus HEAD-bound candidate reproducibility that rely on prose-only constraints. Registry publication, tag and terminal CI are the separate delivery chunk and are correctly represented as pending rather than done.

findings.description: A release_readiness review attempt 03 was requested at this exact source (same checks digest b75e9709), and its prompt plus .checks.json snapshot are retained, but there is no phase-20-attempt-03.json record and no .cli.json output, and docs/phase-status.json release_readiness_attempts (lines 4578-4591) still lists only attempts 01 and 02. The attempt is therefore undisclosed, and tools/review_phase.py:425-426 will refuse to reuse attempt 3 because the prompt already exists, so the delivery instruction in docs/RELEASE.md:42 must use a different NN.
findings.required_fix: Record the actual disposition of readiness attempt 03 in docs/phase-status.json (in-flight, failed, or abandoned, with its preserved prompt/checks paths) and obtain the mandatory accepted current-source readiness review under the next unused attempt number.

findings.description: test_verified_publication_is_consistent_in_current_release_documents returns early whenever the workspace version differs from the last recorded publication, which is the case now (0.2.2 vs 0.2.1). Consequently nothing currently asserts that the current-release receipt links in CHANGELOG.md:6-7 and docs/RELEASE.md:5-6 resolve; both point at docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.2.json and release-tag-v0.2.2.json, which do not yet exist. The dormancy is disclosed in phase-status (finding 5 disposition, lines 4440-4448) and the guard is fixture-tested at tools/test_ci.py:370-410, but the live assertion only activates after registry_publication is recorded.
findings.required_fix: Keep the mandated post-publication sequence (record registry_publication, then execute tools/test_ci.py and preserve its output before the delivery commit), or add a link-existence assertion for the current development version so dangling release-document links cannot ship unnoticed.

findings.description: commands_for(20) reuses commands_for(17), which takes commands_for(12)[4:25] and therefore deliberately excludes scripts/check-package.py. The two clean archive proofs are thus operator-run artifacts rather than gate-executed commands. scripts/check-access-release.py:60-110 mitigates this strongly (archive bytes, inventory, VCS, filesystem and release-commit byte equality, executed-example and consumer assertions), but the recorded `checks` arrays themselves are accepted as evidence of execution, which is the documented repository-writer trust boundary rather than a verified property.
findings.required_fix: No functional change is required for this release; state the package-proof execution boundary where the gate is defined (a comment at tools/check_phase.py:70-87 or docs/PACKAGING.md) so a future maintainer does not read the 59-command gate as including clean packaging.

findings.description: The candidate guard requires proof['releaseCommit'] to equal the current HEAD, so docs/checks/phase-20-candidate.json becomes non-reproducible after any later evidence-only commit. That operational rule currently exists only as prose in docs/phase-status.json delivery_execution_constraints (line 4533, 'do not rerun the HEAD-bound candidate checker after receipt-only delivery commits').
findings.required_fix: Document the HEAD-binding constraint in docs/RELEASE.md alongside the delivery sequence (or accept an explicit --release-commit argument) so the rule is discoverable from the release procedure rather than only from phase bookkeeping.
